record.text: Microscopic animals that can be dried out completely and revived later manage it through protective proteins and genes that switch on as they lose water. What different things do the projects working from these animals try to learn or build out of that ability?
record.reference_answer: Four projects work from these animals, and each takes a different angle on the same ability. BIOSTASIS uses the tardigrade Ramazzottius varieornatus and comparative transcriptomics (RNAseq and ddPCR) across evolutionary lineages within the phylum, looking for gene expression signatures that mark the active, desiccated and rehydrated states. Desiccation Survival works one level down, at the protein level: it asks which sequence features of tardigrade Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) intrinsically disordered proteins drive the glass-transition and gelation that shields other intracellular proteins, screening designed sequence libraries with a survival-based assay and analysing the hits by machine learning. FLINDIP takes the same class of tardigrade disordered proteins as raw material for a different question, mapping genotype to phenotype by deep mutational scanning of hundreds of thousands of variants in competition assays. DRYNET is the applied case: it treats midge and tardigrades as models of reversible drying in order to replace liquid-nitrogen cryopreservation with dry storage of cells and germplasm, loading cells with natural xero-protectants (Late Embryogenesis Abundant proteins) before drying.
record.notes: Seeds from cp6 candidate vector-49 (anhydrobiosis/desiccation survival); candidate evidence SQL re-executed this pass and reproduced exactly 4 projects (734434 DRYNET, 747087 BIOSTASIS, 838945 Desiccation Survival, 898203 FLINDIP). Question tightened from the seed's broad 'desiccation survival' framing to the organism family, because the broad reading also admits DRYSTORE (749537), RESIST (823746) and arguably DormantMicrobes (636928), which would push the gold set past the L2 window. Membership rule: the project's research works from these animals or their molecules. Closed-set proof by exhaustive full-text sweep over the chunk table (objective + all report sections): SELECT project_id FROM chunk WHERE text ILIKE '%tardigrad%' OR text ILIKE '%water bear%' returns exactly these four projects and no others. Second sweep (anhydrobio|cryptobio|desiccation tolerance|desiccation survival|survive desiccation|xeroprotect over chunk.text) returns 734434, 747087, 749537, 823746, 838945; the two extras were read and are OUT - DRYSTORE dries mammalian fibroblasts and gametes with xeroprotectants and never works from these animals, RESIST studies resurrection PLANTS (Haberlea rhodopensis, Xerophyta humilis). Objective/title LIKE sweeps over desiccat/anhydrobio/cryptobio/tardigrad/xeroprotect/dry storage/rehydrat/drying/freeze-dry (19 + 34 rows) surfaced no further animal-desiccation projects; NEMAQUA (696373, rehydrated nematode live feed, a product not a study of the ability), 3F-FutureFreshFruit (656127, fruit cuticle water loss), iDAPT (845799, ice algae cold adaptation), RHEA (725998, bdelloid rotifer asexual genome evolution, desiccation only as a source of DNA breaks) all OUT. record.text: What do EU-funded projects on cancer cachexia identify as the drivers of the wasting of adipose tissue and muscle in cancer patients?
record.reference_answer: Two projects study cancer cachexia head-on and together describe it as a whole-body failure rather than a muscle-local one. CSI-Fun treats cancer associated cachexia (CAC) as a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients and the immediate cause of death for a third of them, and demonstrated experimentally that uncontrolled inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players, with immune cells interacting with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC. StopWaste locates the driver in metabolism: its data support the concept that tumours activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, and the project identified cachexia-specific bioreactive lipids stemming from altered liver lipids and dysregulated liver lipid enzymes, which could be targeted with the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin, plus an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) in cachectic adipose tissue, partly linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. Combining them, the wasting of fat and muscle is driven by inflammation and neuro-endocrine signalling acting on a reprogrammed lipid and glucose metabolism spanning tumour, adipose tissue and liver, with disturbed glucose metabolism appearing early - patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile candidate vector-65 (cachexia). Drift check: `SELECT p.id, p.acronym FROM project p WHERE p.objective ILIKE '%cachexia%' OR p.title ILIKE '%cachexia%'` -> 4 rows (683658 LIFEOMEGA, 741888 CSI-Fun, 897735 REBOOST, 949017 StopWaste), matching the candidate. Read all four: 949017 IN (cachexia is the whole project - futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, ceramides, PDK4); 741888 IN (Cancer associated Cachexia is one of its three named research strands, with mechanism findings on inflammation, the beta-adrenergic system and the sympathetic nervous system); 683658 LIFEOMEGA OUT (an omega-3 EPA food-supplement feasibility study; cachexia named only as a target market for clinical nutrition, no investigation of what drives wasting); 897735 REBOOST OUT (SEPN1-related myopathy; cancer cachexia named once as a condition the model paradigm might later extend to). Pooled adjudications on the 19-project pool for the final question text: 677006 CMIL OUT - its cachexia work is explicitly infection-associated ('T cell responses mediate cachexia during viral infection ... a novel model to study infection-associated cachexia'), not tumour-driven; 818943 UreaCa OUT - the project targets urea-cycle dysregulation in carcinogenesis and reports one incidental downstream result that liver metabolism promotes cancer progression to cachexia, it does not study what drives the wasting; 639548 STARS OUT - thyroid-hormone-driven skeletal muscle wasting across chronic diseases, muscle only, not adipose and not cachexia-targeted; 101033310 Myo_LysoZOOM OUT - lysosomal signalling in muscle wasting generally; 694677 VitruVius OUT - Drosophila growth coordination, host tissue wasting only noted as 'similar to' cancer-induced cachexia; 787041 LIPOMET OUT - lists cancer-associated cachexia as an open future question, no findings; 101003153 FAT-BC, 101020641 PancObese, 748944 LiSDMA, 852086 AGEMEC, 894001 Pept-AGE, 678732 PROMISS, 639382 aCROBAT, 674760 platinDx, 852761 ONco-Energetics_OFF, 964264 TRANSCAN-3, 715575 Reg-Seq, 874708 TheraLymph all OUT on their best chunk (obesity/adiposity, diabetes, sarcopenia, senior malnutrition, brown fat, chemotherapy prediction, tumour bioenergetics, funding coordination, T2D genomics, lymphedema - none about cachexia). evidence:
Gold 741888 CSI-Fun - "Chronic Systemic Inflammation: Functional organ cross-talk in inflammatory disease and cancer". Objective: "The aim of this research proposal is to substantially advance our understanding of whole organ physiology in relation to systemic inflammation as a cause or/and consequence of disease with the focus on Psoriasis/Joint Diseases and Cancer Cachexia. ... such as Inflammatory Skin/Joint disease and Cachexia, a deadly systemic manifestation of Cancer." Report summary: "3. Cancer associated Cachexia (CAC): is a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients, characterized by involuntary loss of body weight due to wasting of muscles and fat. CAC is detrimental to cancer patients' quality of life and considered the immediate cause of death for a third of of cancer patients. ... We studied how uncontrolled inflammation, perturbed hormone balance and the nervous system operate and interact during CAC using model systems that mimic the patient situation. We experimentally demonstrated that inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players that should be closely monitored in patients. In addition, we showed how immune cells interact with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC".

Gold 949017 StopWaste - "Targeting the crosstalk of lipid and glucose metabolism to stop cancer-associated wasting". Objective: "Cachexia is the deadly outcome of many late stage cancers. It is characterized by severe wasting of adipose tissue and muscle mass, cardiac dysfunction and systemic inflammation. ... My current data support the new concept that tumors activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, which leads to an energy crisis that drives systemic metabolic dysfunction. ... perturbed adipose tissue in cachexia causes the increased release of bioreactive signaling lipids such as C16:0 ceramides which appear before any wasting occurs." Report summary: "We have identified bioreactive lipid species specific to cachexia that result from alterations in liver lipids and dysregulation of key enzymes of liver lipid metabolism. We found that these lipids contributed to cachexia by influencing muscle and liver metabolism, and could be targeted using the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin. ... we identified substantial differences between cachectic and non-cachectic adipose tissue, particularly an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA). Dysfunctional adipose tissue metabolism was partially linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. ... patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers".

- 677006 CMIL, lexical rank 2 - workPerformed: "We uncovered a previously unrecognized role by our T cell responses mediate cachexia during viral infection and established a novel model to study infection-associated cachexia (Baazim et al. 2019)". Its cachexia is infection-driven, not tumour-driven. OUT.
- 818943 UreaCa, hybrid rank 7 - workPerformed: "we demonstrate that liver metabolism is affected by extrahepatic cancers leading to systemic changes and promoting cancer progression to cachexia." EPA supports weight management" (a food-supplement feasibility and business study). 897735 REBOOST objective - "other inherited or acquired myopathies sharing an underlying bioenergetic deficiency, including sarcopenia and cancer cachexia" (SEPN1-related myopathy).

record.text: Across EU-funded projects working on quantum key distribution, what kinds of link do they run the keys over - optical fibre, free space, or satellite?
record.reference_answer: European quantum key distribution work divides by the channel the keys travel over. On installed optical fibre, OPENQKD ran an open pan-European testbed, deploying 40 QKD systems over more than 1000km of fibre links with sites in Geneva, Cambridge, Madrid and Poznan; CiViQ drove Continuous-Variable QKD systems and components up to TRL 6 for integration into emerging optical telecommunication networks; and UNIQORN built a pluggable SFP DPS transmitter for low-cost 1-kb/s QKD and ran field trials in the live Smart-City demonstrator Bristol-is-Open. Qurope performed quantum key distribution with entangled photons from quantum dots over a commercially deployed fibre network, including after entanglement swapping, as well as in free space. The free-space and satellite arm is the other half: SatCV implemented a full self-referenced CV-QKD scheme on a free-space channel as a first step towards satellite QKD, QUANGO designed a constellation of 12U-CubeSat low-earth-orbit satellites carrying a QKD payload plus the matching ground stations, and WASPSNEST field-tested its wavelength-tunable single-photon source prototype in a free-space quantum key distribution system.
record.notes: Seeds: the cp6 candidate vector-59 ids, re-confirmed this pass by re-executing its evidence SQL (objective/title ILIKE '%quantum key distribution%' -> 8 rows: 754509 WASPSNEST, 792557 GENIUS, 817021 EQUALITY, 840691 SatCV, 857156 OPENQKD, 899814 Qurope, 101004341 QUANGO, 101025664 QESPEM), all eight read in full before the question existed. Membership criterion applied to every candidate, stated so it has one reading: (a) the project itself works on distributing quantum keys - building, deploying or demonstrating a QKD link or system - and (b) its own text names the physical channel those keys travel over. Seed adjudications: 840691 SatCV IN (self-referenced CV-QKD on a free-space channel, toward satellite); 857156 OPENQKD IN (40 QKD systems, >1000km deployed fibre, ~20 testbed sites); 899814 Qurope IN (QKD with quantum-dot entangled photons over a commercial deployed fibre network and free space); 101004341 QUANGO IN (satellite-to-ground QKD from 12U-CubeSat LEO constellation plus ground stations); 754509 WASPSNEST IN (objective 4 is field-testing the prototype in a free-space QKD system - a component project, but it runs the free-space link); 792557 GENIUS OUT (entropic inequalities and security proofs for QKD rates; no physical channel of its own); 817021 EQUALITY OUT (Innovation-programme market study of Quandela photon emitters, work performed was interviews with QKD network actors, no link built or demonstrated); 101025664 QESPEM OUT (plexcitonic quantum emitters; QKD named only as one application area in a list). Pooled candidates added by retrieval and accepted after reading: 820466 CiViQ IN (CV-QKD to TRL 6, validation in a true telecom network environment), 820474 UNIQORN IN (SFP QKD transmitter, system evaluation in real fibre networks, Bristol-is-Open field trials). Pooled candidates rejected on their best chunk as classical optical communication with no quantum keys: 848413 OpticalSpaceLink, 813236 FREESPACE, 775768 RAVEN, 804769 COYOTE, 838143 ReSOLeS, 821878 SODaH, 724663 InnoSpace. Rejected after reading, as quantum work that distributes no keys: 894590 QSPACE (space-compatible quantum memories), 845255 QuaIL, 792727 SMERC, 862721 QuanTELCO (telecom-band spin centres, benchmarks spin-photon entanglement over urban fibre, not keys), 840958 ADOQ (entanglement through turbulent media; never says QKD or quantum key in its objective), 675662 QCALL (doctoral training network; its own contribution is protocol analysis and training, it commits to no channel of its own). record.text: Microscopic animals that can be dried out completely and revived later manage it through protective proteins and genes that switch on as they lose water. What different things do the projects working from these animals try to learn or build out of that ability?
record.reference_answer: Four projects work from these animals, and each takes a different angle on the same ability. BIOSTASIS uses the tardigrade Ramazzottius varieornatus and comparative transcriptomics (RNAseq and ddPCR) across evolutionary lineages within the phylum, looking for gene expression signatures that mark the active, desiccated and rehydrated states. Desiccation Survival works one level down, at the protein level: it asks which sequence features of tardigrade Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) intrinsically disordered proteins drive the glass-transition and gelation that shields other intracellular proteins, screening designed sequence libraries with a survival-based assay and analysing the hits by machine learning. FLINDIP takes the same class of tardigrade disordered proteins as raw material for a different question, mapping genotype to phenotype by deep mutational scanning of hundreds of thousands of variants in competition assays. DRYNET is the applied case: it treats midge and tardigrades as models of reversible drying in order to replace liquid-nitrogen cryopreservation with dry storage of cells and germplasm, loading cells with natural xero-protectants (Late Embryogenesis Abundant proteins) before drying.
record.notes: Seeds from cp6 candidate vector-49 (anhydrobiosis/desiccation survival); candidate evidence SQL re-executed this pass and reproduced exactly 4 projects (734434 DRYNET, 747087 BIOSTASIS, 838945 Desiccation Survival, 898203 FLINDIP). Question tightened from the seed's broad 'desiccation survival' framing to the organism family, because the broad reading also admits DRYSTORE (749537), RESIST (823746) and arguably DormantMicrobes (636928), which would push the gold set past the L2 window. Membership rule: the project's research works from these animals or their molecules. Closed-set proof by exhaustive full-text sweep over the chunk table (objective + all report sections): SELECT project_id FROM chunk WHERE text ILIKE '%tardigrad%' OR text ILIKE '%water bear%' returns exactly these four projects and no others. Second sweep (anhydrobio|cryptobio|desiccation tolerance|desiccation survival|survive desiccation|xeroprotect over chunk.text) returns 734434, 747087, 749537, 823746, 838945; the two extras were read and are OUT - DRYSTORE dries mammalian fibroblasts and gametes with xeroprotectants and never works from these animals, RESIST studies resurrection PLANTS (Haberlea rhodopensis, Xerophyta humilis). Objective/title LIKE sweeps over desiccat/anhydrobio/cryptobio/tardigrad/xeroprotect/dry storage/rehydrat/drying/freeze-dry (19 + 34 rows) surfaced no further animal-desiccation projects; NEMAQUA (696373, rehydrated nematode live feed, a product not a study of the ability), 3F-FutureFreshFruit (656127, fruit cuticle water loss), iDAPT (845799, ice algae cold adaptation), RHEA (725998, bdelloid rotifer asexual genome evolution, desiccation only as a source of DNA breaks) all OUT. Pooled adjudication of the 25-project pool: 734434 IN (report: new genes for reversible drying discovered 'on our model (midge and tardigrades)'), 747087 IN, 838945 IN; all 22 others OUT on their best chunk as off-topic, with DRYSTORE, RESIST and DormantMicrobes (636928, dormant soil microorganisms) read in full and rejected for the reasons above. 898203 FLINDIP is a seed that no condition retrieved at k=10 in any of the three phrasings tried - kept in gold because its text plainly satisfies the question ('We plan to focus on tardigrade proteins which are essential for their ability to survive complete desiccation'; report: 'disordered proteins that contribute to surviving complete desiccation in their host organisms') and retrieval never decides truth. term_style=paraphrase: the question uses none of the gold texts' key terms (tardigrade, anhydrobiosis, cryptobiosis, desiccation, intrinsically disordered); the rank matrix agrees - lexical retrieved NONE of the gold projects, all three retrieved gold came via dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank. Two earlier phrasings were discarded: a broad 'cells and tiny animals dried out completely' version (gold set too large for L2) and a 'water bears' version whose meta-framing retrieved only 1 of 4 seeds.

Per gold project, the passages that satisfy the question (verbatim):

**747087 BIOSTASIS** - objective: "The current proposal uses tardigrades as a model to gain novel insight into molecular signatures underlying this unique biological phenomenon. ... I will use transcriptome sequencing (RNAseq) and ddPCR to reveal key-player genes and characterize functional pathways involved in i) different stages of anhydrobiosis of single tardigrade species and ii) between different evolutionary lineages within the phylum." Report summary: "The project results revealed that the duration of the desiccation stress impacts both the total number of genes that are regulated at the 'tun state' and also the recovery time needed for the individuals to return to their normal gene expression levels".

**838945 Desiccation Survival** - objective: "Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) proteins, a family of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) in tardigrades (a phylum of micro-animals), have been shown to be important for their survival during long periods of dryness. ... I aim to unravel the sequence determinants of CAHS protein functions ... (ii) screen the library with a high-throughput survival-based assay and validate the hits both in vitro and in vivo; (iii) analyse the results with machine learning algorithms".

**898203 FLINDIP** - objective: "We plan to focus on tardigrade proteins which are essential for their ability to survive complete desiccation. We plan to generate libraries of cells expressing hundreds of thousands of variants of these proteins and to perform competition assays to measure functionality of every variant in the library." Report summary: "We are focusing on disordered proteins that contribute to surviving complete desiccation in their host organisms."

**734434 DRYNET** - objective: "DRYNET's relies on water subtraction to induce a reversible block of metabolism, a survival strategy available in nature (anhydrobiosis). The work plan foresees the exploitation of natural xero-protectants (Late Embryogenesis Abundant proteins), loaded/expressed in gametes/cells, before drying." Report summary: "New models for controlled de-hydration of cells, new genes and related gene products for reversible drying have been discovered on our model (midge and tardigrades)."

- **636928 DormantMicrobes** - OUT. "much of this functional redundancy is embodied in non-active, dormant microorganisms". Soil microbial dormancy/resuscitation, not drying-and-revival of animals.

record.text: What do EU-funded projects on cancer cachexia identify as the drivers of the wasting of adipose tissue and muscle in cancer patients?
record.reference_answer: Two projects study cancer cachexia head-on and together describe it as a whole-body failure rather than a muscle-local one. CSI-Fun treats cancer associated cachexia (CAC) as a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients and the immediate cause of death for a third of them, and demonstrated experimentally that uncontrolled inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players, with immune cells interacting with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC. StopWaste locates the driver in metabolism: its data support the concept that tumours activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, and the project identified cachexia-specific bioreactive lipids stemming from altered liver lipids and dysregulated liver lipid enzymes, which could be targeted with the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin, plus an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) in cachectic adipose tissue, partly linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. Combining them, the wasting of fat and muscle is driven by inflammation and neuro-endocrine signalling acting on a reprogrammed lipid and glucose metabolism spanning tumour, adipose tissue and liver, with disturbed glucose metabolism appearing early - patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers.

evidence:
Gold 741888 CSI-Fun - "Chronic Systemic Inflammation: Functional organ cross-talk in inflammatory disease and cancer". Objective: "The aim of this research proposal is to substantially advance our understanding of whole organ physiology in relation to systemic inflammation as a cause or/and consequence of disease with the focus on Psoriasis/Joint Diseases and Cancer Cachexia. ... such as Inflammatory Skin/Joint disease and Cachexia, a deadly systemic manifestation of Cancer." Report summary: "3. Cancer associated Cachexia (CAC): is a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients, characterized by involuntary loss of body weight due to wasting of muscles and fat. CAC is detrimental to cancer patients' quality of life and considered the immediate cause of death for a third of of cancer patients. ... We studied how uncontrolled inflammation, perturbed hormone balance and the nervous system operate and interact during CAC using model systems that mimic the patient situation. We experimentally demonstrated that inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players that should be closely monitored in patients. In addition, we showed how immune cells interact with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC".

Gold 949017 StopWaste - "Targeting the crosstalk of lipid and glucose metabolism to stop cancer-associated wasting". Objective: "Cachexia is the deadly outcome of many late stage cancers. It is characterized by severe wasting of adipose tissue and muscle mass, cardiac dysfunction and systemic inflammation. ... My current data support the new concept that tumors activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, which leads to an energy crisis that drives systemic metabolic dysfunction. ... perturbed adipose tissue in cachexia causes the increased release of bioreactive signaling lipids such as C16:0 ceramides which appear before any wasting occurs." Report summary: "We have identified bioreactive lipid species specific to cachexia that result from alterations in liver lipids and dysregulation of key enzymes of liver lipid metabolism. We found that these lipids contributed to cachexia by influencing muscle and liver metabolism, and could be targeted using the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin. ... we identified substantial differences between cachectic and non-cachectic adipose tissue, particularly an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA). Dysfunctional adipose tissue metabolism was partially linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. ... patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers".

- 818943 UreaCa, hybrid rank 7 - workPerformed: "we demonstrate that liver metabolism is affected by extrahepatic cancers leading to systemic changes and promoting cancer progression to cachexia." record.text: Microscopic animals that can be dried out completely and revived later manage it through protective proteins and genes that switch on as they lose water. What different things do the projects working from these animals try to learn or build out of that ability?
record.reference_answer: Four projects work from these animals, and each takes a different angle on the same ability. BIOSTASIS uses the tardigrade Ramazzottius varieornatus and comparative transcriptomics (RNAseq and ddPCR) across evolutionary lineages within the phylum, looking for gene expression signatures that mark the active, desiccated and rehydrated states. Desiccation Survival works one level down, at the protein level: it asks which sequence features of tardigrade Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) intrinsically disordered proteins drive the glass-transition and gelation that shields other intracellular proteins, screening designed sequence libraries with a survival-based assay and analysing the hits by machine learning. FLINDIP takes the same class of tardigrade disordered proteins as raw material for a different question, mapping genotype to phenotype by deep mutational scanning of hundreds of thousands of variants in competition assays. DRYNET is the applied case: it treats midge and tardigrades as models of reversible drying in order to replace liquid-nitrogen cryopreservation with dry storage of cells and germplasm, loading cells with natural xero-protectants (Late Embryogenesis Abundant proteins) before drying.

record.text: Across EU-funded projects working on quantum key distribution, what kinds of link do they run the keys over - optical fibre, free space, or satellite?
record.reference_answer: European quantum key distribution work divides by the channel the keys travel over. On installed optical fibre, OPENQKD ran an open pan-European testbed, deploying 40 QKD systems over more than 1000km of fibre links with sites in Geneva, Cambridge, Madrid and Poznan; CiViQ drove Continuous-Variable QKD systems and components up to TRL 6 for integration into emerging optical telecommunication networks; and UNIQORN built a pluggable SFP DPS transmitter for low-cost 1-kb/s QKD and ran field trials in the live Smart-City demonstrator Bristol-is-Open. Qurope performed quantum key distribution with entangled photons from quantum dots over a commercially deployed fibre network, including after entanglement swapping, as well as in free space. The free-space and satellite arm is the other half: SatCV implemented a full self-referenced CV-QKD scheme on a free-space channel as a first step towards satellite QKD, QUANGO designed a constellation of 12U-CubeSat low-earth-orbit satellites carrying a QKD payload plus the matching ground stations, and WASPSNEST field-tested its wavelength-tunable single-photon source prototype in a free-space quantum key distribution system.

evidence:
Gold, with the passages that satisfy "what kind of link do they run the keys over":

- **857156 OPENQKD** (Open European Quantum Key Distribution Testbed) - objective: "OPENQKD will deploy 40 QKD systems with standardized hardware and software interfaces for network devices and protocols on over 1000km of fiber links, as well as testing compatibility with satellite-based schemes." ... "we will incorporate testbeds in Cambridge (UK), Madrid (ES) and Poznan (PL)" alongside "a central QKD testbed in Geneva (CH)". Report summary: "the OPENQKD project set up many testbed sites across Europe (approx. 20 different locations) ... with deployed optical fiber infrastructure and locations at the end-user premises".
- **820466 CiViQ** (Continuous Variable Quantum Communications) - objective: "The goal of the CiViQ project is to open a radically novel avenue towards flexible and cost-effective integration of quantum communication technologies, and in particular Continuous-Variable QKD, into emerging optical telecommunication networks." ... "Drive CV-QKD systems and components up to TRL 6" ... "CiViQ will culminate in a validation in true telecom network environment."
- **820474 UNIQORN** - objective: "the first DPS transmitter as pluggable SFP module for low-cost 1-kb/s QKD" ... "Network-integration and system evaluation in real fibre networks will be enabled by quantum-aware software defined networking and field trials in the live Smart-City demonstrator Bristol-is-Open." Report workPerformed: "several use-cases for QKD were identified ranging from securing 5G installations to fiber-to-the-home applications."
- **899814 Qurope** (Quantum Repeaters using On-demand Photonic Entanglement) - report workPerformed: "we have achieved our goals in work package 3 and showed quantum key distribution using entangled photons emitted from quantum dots in a fiber network as well as free-space (back-to-back publications in science advances). findings.claim: WASPSNEST (754509) ran keys over no link: its own report states the free-space QKD field test was never started, so it does not satisfy a question asking what kind of link these projects run the keys over.
findings.evidence: Full get_project_text([754509]). The objective (a 12-month FET Innovation Launchpad for a single-photon source) lists 'testing of the prototype in a free-space quantum key distribution system' as PLANNED work, and report summary objective 4 repeats it as an aim. Report workPerformed: 'This was a short (12 month) project which was substantively hindered by a delay in hiring a postdoctoral researcher ... Work on the module alignment protocol was commenced in the final 3 months of the project and further work is required to complete this task. Field testing and advancing commercial arrangements require the module alignment task to be complete so we have not yet been in a position to commence those tasks.' finalResults confirms only materials/lifetime advances. findings.fix_direction: Drop 754509 from gold_project_ids and pooling_evidence.accepted (6 remain, L3 holds), move it to the OUT list in notes with the workPerformed quote as the reason, and delete the WASPSNEST clause from the reference answer.

The objective future-tense plan is the only textual basis for the reference past-tense claim.
findings.fix_direction: Remove the clause with the gold member, or - if WASPSNEST is kept on an intent reading - reword to the honest form ('intended a free-space QKD field test but reported that the test was never started'), which also changes what the question measures for that member.

judge_decisions.rationale: All three findings are one root defect: the membership rule that makes this a survey of operating QKD links is recorded in notes instead of in the question, so the gold contains a project that never ran a link and excludes a project that satisfies the looser wording. The question is meant to measure whether a condition can pool five-plus projects and map each to the physical channel its keys travel over; that measurement is intact, and the fix is bounded - one wording change plus two gold/reference edits that follow from it. Every option leaves |gold| >= 5, so the vector L3 / survey cell does not move.

record.text: Which projects are developing ways to pull the plant nutrients out of livestock slurry and dung and concentrate them into a fertiliser product that can be stored and handled like a bought fertiliser, instead of the raw waste simply being spread on nearby fields?
record.reference_answer: Twelve projects treat livestock manure or slurry as a raw material and pull its nitrogen and phosphorus into a fertiliser that can be stored, moved and sold, rather than spread raw under the EU Nitrates Directive limits. Separation and drying routes: UltraBio splits manure and digestate with ultrasound so most nutrients bind to a solid product that is pelletised and sold as a storable organic fertiliser while the liquid can be released; ENFIR dehydrates manure with far-infrared heat into pelletized compost, producing more than 1.500 ton/year of organic fertilizer per unit; IMBIO processes animal waste including chicken manure into organic fertilizers for small and medium farms. Nitrogen-capture routes: Poul-AR biologically converts poultry manure's organic nitrogen to ammonia, strips it with air and fixes it with sulphuric or nitric acid as an ammonium salt fertilizer; AMBIENCE captures 70% - 80% of the ammonia from pig farms and biogas plant digestate with permeable membranes and delivers Ammonia Sulphate (NH4)2SO4 for fertilizer manufacturers. Whole-plant recovery: FERTIMANURE runs 5 on-farm pilots and targets 31 marketable end-products; DEPURGAN's electrocoagulation reactor yields a solid fraction with calorific potential plus an NPK liquid effluent; SYSTEMIC processes digestate of pig manure into a mineral N fertiliser, an organic soil improver and a P fertiliser, explicitly to reduce the import of P as a finite resource from mines. Manure is one feedstock among several in NewFert (ashes of different origins and livestock effluents into a new generation of fertilisers) and B-FERST (struvite from pig slurries, plus ashes and compost, into 8 specialised fertilisers). VALI and SUSTAINABLEFARM pair energy recovery with a fertiliser product - VALI burns manure for heat and electricity leaving compact, easy-to-transport ashes directly usable as dry fertilizer, and SUSTAINABLEFARM converts manure into biogas and organic fertilizers.

record.text: Some barrel-shaped micro-animals with eight stubby clawed legs can dry out completely and start living again when rewetted. Among the projects that use these particular animals, or proteins taken from them, as their experimental material, what different things does each try to learn or build out of that ability?
record.reference_answer: Four projects work from these animals, and each takes a different angle on the same ability. BIOSTASIS uses the tardigrade Ramazzottius varieornatus and comparative transcriptomics (RNAseq and ddPCR) across evolutionary lineages within the phylum, looking for gene expression signatures that mark the active, desiccated and rehydrated states. Desiccation Survival works one level down, at the protein level: it asks which sequence features of tardigrade Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) intrinsically disordered proteins drive the glass-transition and gelation that shields other intracellular proteins, screening designed sequence libraries with a survival-based assay and analysing the hits by machine learning. FLINDIP takes the same class of tardigrade disordered proteins as raw material for a different question, mapping genotype to phenotype by deep mutational scanning of hundreds of thousands of variants in competition assays. DRYNET is the applied case: it treats midge and tardigrades as models of reversible drying in order to replace liquid-nitrogen cryopreservation with dry storage of cells and germplasm, loading cells with natural xero-protectants (Late Embryogenesis Abundant proteins) before drying.
record.notes: Seeds from cp6 candidate vector-49; candidate evidence SQL re-executed this pass, reproducing exactly 4 projects (734434 DRYNET, 747087 BIOSTASIS, 838945 Desiccation Survival, 898203 FLINDIP). record.text: What do EU-funded projects on cancer cachexia identify as the drivers of the wasting of adipose tissue and muscle in cancer patients?
record.reference_answer: Two projects study cancer cachexia head-on and together describe it as a whole-body failure rather than a muscle-local one. CSI-Fun treats cancer associated cachexia (CAC) as a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients and the immediate cause of death for a third of them, and demonstrated experimentally that uncontrolled inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players, with immune cells interacting with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC. StopWaste locates the driver in metabolism: its data support the concept that tumours activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, and the project identified cachexia-specific bioreactive lipids stemming from altered liver lipids and dysregulated liver lipid enzymes, which could be targeted with the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin, plus an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) in cachectic adipose tissue, partly linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. Combining them, the wasting of fat and muscle is driven by inflammation and neuro-endocrine signalling acting on a reprogrammed lipid and glucose metabolism spanning tumour, adipose tissue and liver, with disturbed glucose metabolism appearing early - patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers.

record.text: Among EU-funded projects that actually build or demonstrate quantum key distribution links rather than only studying them, what kinds of channel do the keys travel over?
record.reference_answer: The projects that actually put keys on a channel divide between installed optical fibre and free space. On fibre, OPENQKD deployed 40 QKD systems over more than 1000km of fibre links across approximately 20 testbed sites, with a central testbed in Geneva (CH) and further ones in Cambridge (UK), Madrid (ES) and Poznan (PL); CiViQ drove Continuous-Variable QKD systems and components up to TRL 6 and validated them in a true telecom network environment, while also preparing next-generation technologies aimed at quantum communication over global distances; and UNIQORN built a pluggable SFP DPS transmitter for low-cost 1-kb/s QKD, evaluated in real fibre networks with field trials in the live Smart-City demonstrator Bristol-is-Open. Qurope spans both channels, performing quantum key distribution with entangled photons from quantum dots over a commercially deployed fibre network, including after entanglement swapping, as well as in free space. The purely free-space work is SPQRel, which developed a free-space quantum communication channel and performed quantum key distribution experiments distributing entangled photons from quantum dots across two buildings a few hundred meters apart in an urban communication scenario, and SatCV, which implemented a full self-referenced CV-QKD scheme on a free-space channel as a first step towards a future satellite implementation.

record.text: Some barrel-shaped micro-animals with eight stubby clawed legs can dry out completely and start living again when rewetted. Among the projects that use these particular animals, or proteins taken from them, as their experimental material, what different things does each try to learn or build out of that ability?
record.reference_answer: Four projects work from these animals, and each takes a different angle on the same ability. BIOSTASIS uses the tardigrade Ramazzottius varieornatus and comparative transcriptomics (RNAseq and ddPCR) across evolutionary lineages within the phylum, looking for gene expression signatures that mark the active, desiccated and rehydrated states. Desiccation Survival works one level down, at the protein level: it asks which sequence features of tardigrade Cytosolic Abundant Heat Soluble (CAHS) intrinsically disordered proteins drive the glass-transition and gelation that shields other intracellular proteins, screening designed sequence libraries with a survival-based assay and analysing the hits by machine learning. FLINDIP takes the same class of tardigrade disordered proteins as raw material for a different question, mapping genotype to phenotype by deep mutational scanning of hundreds of thousands of variants in competition assays. DRYNET is the applied case: it treats midge and tardigrades as models of reversible drying in order to replace liquid-nitrogen cryopreservation with dry storage of cells and germplasm, loading cells with natural xero-protectants (Late Embryogenesis Abundant proteins) before drying.
record.notes: Seeds from cp6 candidate vector-49; candidate evidence SQL re-executed this pass, reproducing exactly 4 projects (734434 DRYNET, 747087 BIOSTASIS, 838945 Desiccation Survival, 898203 FLINDIP). MEMBERSHIP IS IN THE QUESTION TEXT: the referent is narrowed by physical traits (barrel-shaped, eight stubby clawed legs) to tardigrades specifically, and the condition 'use these particular animals, or proteins taken from them, as their experimental material' is stated in the question rather than held in these notes. That makes both boundary calls derivable by a solver: DRYNET is IN because its report records that new genes for reversible drying were discovered 'on our model (midge and tardigrades)'; DRYSTORE (749537) is OUT because its material is mammalian fibroblasts and gametes protected by xeroprotectants, with no material taken from these animals anywhere in its stored text; RHEA (725998) is OUT because its animals are bdelloid rotifers, which have a ciliated wheel organ and no legs and so are not the animals described. (1) Term route: SELECT project_id FROM chunk WHERE text ILIKE '%tardigrad%' OR text ILIKE '%water bear%' returns exactly 734434, 747087, 838945, 898203 over objective and all report sections. record.text: What do EU-funded projects on cancer cachexia identify as the drivers of the wasting of adipose tissue and muscle in cancer patients?
record.reference_answer: Two projects study cancer cachexia head-on and together describe it as a whole-body failure rather than a muscle-local one. CSI-Fun treats cancer associated cachexia (CAC) as a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients and the immediate cause of death for a third of them, and demonstrated experimentally that uncontrolled inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players, with immune cells interacting with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC. StopWaste locates the driver in metabolism: its data support the concept that tumours activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, and the project identified cachexia-specific bioreactive lipids stemming from altered liver lipids and dysregulated liver lipid enzymes, which could be targeted with the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin, plus an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) in cachectic adipose tissue, partly linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. Combining them, the wasting of fat and muscle is driven by inflammation and neuro-endocrine signalling acting on a reprogrammed lipid and glucose metabolism spanning tumour, adipose tissue and liver, with disturbed glucose metabolism appearing early - patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile candidate vector-65 (cachexia). Drift check: `SELECT p.id, p.acronym FROM project p WHERE p.objective ILIKE '%cachexia%' OR p.title ILIKE '%cachexia%'` -> 4 rows (683658 LIFEOMEGA, 741888 CSI-Fun, 897735 REBOOST, 949017 StopWaste), matching the candidate. Read all four: 949017 IN (cachexia is the whole project - futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, ceramides, PDK4); 741888 IN (Cancer associated Cachexia is one of its three named research strands, with mechanism findings on inflammation, the beta-adrenergic system and the sympathetic nervous system); 683658 LIFEOMEGA OUT (an omega-3 EPA food-supplement feasibility study; cachexia named only as a target market for clinical nutrition, no investigation of what drives wasting); 897735 REBOOST OUT (SEPN1-related myopathy; cancer cachexia named once as a condition the model paradigm might later extend to). The gold boundary is drawn on what the question asks - the drivers of the wasting of ADIPOSE TISSUE and MUSCLE - not on whether a project mentions or even works on cachexia. Pooled adjudications on the 19-project pool for the final question text: 818943 UreaCa OUT, and this is the closest call, so the ground is stated exactly. UreaCa's cachexia work is NOT incidental - it is a headline outcome of the project: finalResults report that 're-expressing HNF4a restricted tumor growth and the development of cachexia manifestations' and that 'our results, supported by ERC-PoC, led to a patent and the establishment of a new company - Metabocure, which will evaluate the potential benefit of mRNA of HNF4a delivered via lipid nanoparticles in alleviating cancer cachexia in mice and human'. It is excluded because across its ENTIRE stored text (objective, summary, workPerformed, finalResults, teaser) UreaCa speaks only of whole-organism 'cachexia manifestations' and 'cachexia symptoms' and never localises its HNF4a / liver-metabolism driver to adipose tissue or muscle, which is the tissue-level account this question asks for; a re-deriver who reads the finalResults should therefore not be surprised into reopening the boundary. 677006 CMIL OUT on the cancer/infection split, not on topical absence: CMIL does study cachexia in adipose and muscle tissue ('we became interested into systemic immunometabolic changes and took a particular focus on adipose and muscle tissue'), but the cachexia it experimentally drives and models is infection-associated - 'T cell responses mediate cachexia during viral infection and established a novel model to study infection-associated cachexia' - whereas the question asks about cancer patients. 639548 STARS OUT - thyroid-hormone-driven skeletal muscle wasting across chronic diseases, muscle only, not adipose and not cachexia-targeted; 101033310 Myo_LysoZOOM OUT - lysosomal signalling in muscle wasting generally; 694677 VitruVius OUT - Drosophila growth coordination, host tissue wasting only noted as 'similar to' cancer-induced cachexia; 787041 LIPOMET OUT - lists cancer-associated cachexia as an open future question, no findings; 101003153 FAT-BC, 101020641 PancObese, 748944 LiSDMA, 852086 AGEMEC, 894001 Pept-AGE, 678732 PROMISS, 639382 aCROBAT, 674760 platinDx, 852761 ONco-Energetics_OFF, 964264 TRANSCAN-3, 715575 Reg-Seq, 874708 TheraLymph all OUT on their best chunk (obesity/adiposity, diabetes, sarcopenia, senior malnutrition, brown fat, chemotherapy prediction, tumour bioenergetics, funding coordination, T2D genomics, lymphedema - none about cachexia). evidence:
Gold 741888 CSI-Fun - "Chronic Systemic Inflammation: Functional organ cross-talk in inflammatory disease and cancer". Objective: "The aim of this research proposal is to substantially advance our understanding of whole organ physiology in relation to systemic inflammation as a cause or/and consequence of disease with the focus on Psoriasis/Joint Diseases and Cancer Cachexia. ... such as Inflammatory Skin/Joint disease and Cachexia, a deadly systemic manifestation of Cancer." Report summary: "3. Cancer associated Cachexia (CAC): is a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients, characterized by involuntary loss of body weight due to wasting of muscles and fat. CAC is detrimental to cancer patients' quality of life and considered the immediate cause of death for a third of of cancer patients. ... We studied how uncontrolled inflammation, perturbed hormone balance and the nervous system operate and interact during CAC using model systems that mimic the patient situation. We experimentally demonstrated that inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players that should be closely monitored in patients. In addition, we showed how immune cells interact with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC".

Gold 949017 StopWaste - "Targeting the crosstalk of lipid and glucose metabolism to stop cancer-associated wasting". Objective: "Cachexia is the deadly outcome of many late stage cancers. It is characterized by severe wasting of adipose tissue and muscle mass, cardiac dysfunction and systemic inflammation. ... My current data support the new concept that tumors activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, which leads to an energy crisis that drives systemic metabolic dysfunction. ... perturbed adipose tissue in cachexia causes the increased release of bioreactive signaling lipids such as C16:0 ceramides which appear before any wasting occurs." Report summary: "We have identified bioreactive lipid species specific to cachexia that result from alterations in liver lipids and dysregulation of key enzymes of liver lipid metabolism. We found that these lipids contributed to cachexia by influencing muscle and liver metabolism, and could be targeted using the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin. ... we identified substantial differences between cachectic and non-cachectic adipose tissue, particularly an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA). Dysfunctional adipose tissue metabolism was partially linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. ... patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers".

Discrimination counter-examples (the four nearest rejects, all pooled top-10 in at least one condition):
- 677006 CMIL, lexical rank 2 - workPerformed: "We uncovered a previously unrecognized role by our T cell responses mediate cachexia during viral infection and established a novel model to study infection-associated cachexia (Baazim et al. 2019)". Its cachexia is infection-driven, not tumour-driven. OUT.
- 818943 UreaCa, hybrid rank 7 - workPerformed: "we demonstrate that liver metabolism is affected by extrahepatic cancers leading to systemic changes and promoting cancer progression to cachexia." One downstream result of a urea-cycle-in-carcinogenesis project, not a study of what drives the wasting. OUT.
- 639548 STARS, lexical rank 3 - objective: "Skeletal muscle wasting is a devastating complication of many chronic diseases including cancer, diabetes, chronic heart failure and cystic fibrosis." Muscle only, thyroid-hormone therapy angle, not cachexia-targeted and silent on adipose. OUT.
- 694677 VitruVius, hybrid_rerank rank 5 - workPerformed: "We have identified a hormone sequestration mechanism linking tumor growth and host tissue wasting, similar to what is observed during cancer-induced cachexia". Drosophila body-size work; the cachexia link is an analogy. OUT.

Seed rejects from the candidate's own four: 683658 LIFEOMEGA objective - "most of cancer patients suffer cachexia or anorexia. EPA supports weight management" (a food-supplement feasibility and business study). 897735 REBOOST objective - "other inherited or acquired myopathies sharing an underlying bioenergetic deficiency, including sarcopenia and cancer cachexia" (SEPN1-related myopathy).

It fills the medical-and-health-sciences / clinical-medicine bucket on the vector L2 synthesis cell with an exact-term topic, an axis the bank has not covered. The L2 label is arithmetic, not asserted: exactly two projects study what drives the wasting, and the synthesis label is honest because neither gold project alone gives the account - CSI-Fun supplies the inflammatory and neuro-endocrine drivers and StopWaste the lipid-glucose metabolic ones, and the answer has to fuse them rather than contrast them.

findings.claim: The new gold boundary is stated as a property of the DRIVER ('never localises its HNF4a / liver-metabolism driver to adipose tissue or muscle'), but under that test gold member 741888 CSI-Fun fails identically - its driver is also stated at whole-organism level. The gold set is correct; the recorded reason for it does not re-derive it.
findings.evidence: Full get_project_text([741888]). CSI-Fun's report summary strand 3: 'Cancer associated Cachexia (CAC): is a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients ... We experimentally demonstrated that inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players'. Nowhere does CSI-Fun tie inflammation or beta-adrenergic signalling to a measurement in adipose tissue or muscle; the driver is attributed to CAC as a whole-body disorder, exactly the level at which UreaCa's workPerformed operates. The contrast that DOES hold: CSI-Fun defines the thing it is explaining as 'wasting of muscles and fat' and StopWaste goes to tissue-level mechanism ('elevated ceramides cause muscle atrophy'; 'substantial differences between cachectic and non-cachectic adipose tissue ... partially linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4'), while UreaCa names the thing it explains only as 'cachexia manifestations' and 'cachexia symptoms' - the strings 'adipose', 'muscle' and 'wasting' occur nowhere in its objective or its four report fields.
findings.fix_direction: A one-sentence rewording of the boundary sentence in notes, no change to gold, level, subtype, term_style, reference answer or question text: draw the line on what each project names as the phenomenon it explains - IN when it identifies the loss of adipose tissue and/or muscle as the thing its driver accounts for, OUT when its account stops at undifferentiated whole-organism 'cachexia manifestations'. The critic marks this advisory and cheap, and says the judge may reasonably decide the current wording is close enough not to spend a round.

judge_decisions.rationale: The question measures whether a vector condition can pool two projects and synthesize the drivers of adipose and muscle wasting, and it still does: the critic's own corpus-exhaustive sweep (9 cachexia projects, all adjudicated) closes the gold set, and its full read confirms 818943 never localises its driver to adipose tissue or muscle, so |gold| = 2 and the L2 synthesis cell are right. record.text: Which projects are developing ways to pull the plant nutrients out of livestock slurry and dung and concentrate them into a fertiliser product that can be stored and handled like a bought fertiliser, instead of the raw waste simply being spread on nearby fields?
record.reference_answer: Twelve projects treat livestock manure or slurry as a raw material and pull its nitrogen and phosphorus into a fertiliser that can be stored, moved and sold, rather than spread raw under the EU Nitrates Directive limits. Separation and drying routes: UltraBio splits manure and digestate with ultrasound so most nutrients bind to a solid product that is pelletised and sold as a storable organic fertiliser while the liquid can be released; ENFIR dehydrates manure with far-infrared heat into pelletized compost, producing more than 1.500 ton/year of organic fertilizer per unit; IMBIO processes animal waste including chicken manure into organic fertilizers for small and medium farms. Nitrogen-capture routes: Poul-AR biologically converts poultry manure's organic nitrogen to ammonia, strips it with air and fixes it with sulphuric or nitric acid as an ammonium salt fertilizer; AMBIENCE captures 70% - 80% of the ammonia from pig farms and biogas plant digestate with permeable membranes and delivers Ammonia Sulphate (NH4)2SO4 for fertilizer manufacturers. Whole-plant recovery: FERTIMANURE runs 5 on-farm pilots and targets 31 marketable end-products; DEPURGAN's electrocoagulation reactor yields a solid fraction with calorific potential plus an NPK liquid effluent; SYSTEMIC processes digestate of pig manure into a mineral N fertiliser, an organic soil improver and a P fertiliser, explicitly to reduce the import of P as a finite resource from mines. Manure is one feedstock among several in NewFert (ashes of different origins and livestock effluents into a new generation of fertilisers) and B-FERST (struvite from pig slurries, plus ashes and compost, into 8 specialised fertilisers). VALI and SUSTAINABLEFARM pair energy recovery with a fertiliser product - VALI burns manure for heat and electricity leaving compact, easy-to-transport ashes directly usable as dry fertilizer, and SUSTAINABLEFARM converts manure into biogas and organic fertilizers.

why_good: The question discriminates on two axes at once: it names none of the corpus's own topic labels (struvite, nutrient recovery, valorisation, digestate, bio-based fertiliser), and five of its twelve gold projects sit outside every condition's top-15, so a condition's score depends on whether it can reach ENFIR, IMBIO, AMBIENCE, VALI and Poul-AR from plain-language wording rather than on word overlap. It also has a hard discrimination edge: the corpus contains a whole family of manure projects that treat, acidify, dose or plasma-upgrade the slurry without ever making a separate product (Treat2ReUse, GasAbate N+, NITROBIO, SmartNitroFarm), so a system that answers on topic similarity rather than on what the text says the project produces will over-collect. On coverage it fills branch=engineering / bucket=environmental-engineering / topic=nutrient-recovery at the vector L3 survey cell with term_style=paraphrase. The L3 label is arithmetic: |gold| = 12.

record.text: What do EU-funded projects on cancer cachexia identify as the drivers of the wasting of adipose tissue and muscle in cancer patients?
record.reference_answer: Two projects study cancer cachexia head-on and together describe it as a whole-body failure rather than a muscle-local one. CSI-Fun treats cancer associated cachexia (CAC) as a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients and the immediate cause of death for a third of them, and demonstrated experimentally that uncontrolled inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players, with immune cells interacting with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC. StopWaste locates the driver in metabolism: its data support the concept that tumours activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, and the project identified cachexia-specific bioreactive lipids stemming from altered liver lipids and dysregulated liver lipid enzymes, which could be targeted with the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin, plus an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) in cachectic adipose tissue, partly linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. Combining them, the wasting of fat and muscle is driven by inflammation and neuro-endocrine signalling acting on a reprogrammed lipid and glucose metabolism spanning tumour, adipose tissue and liver, with disturbed glucose metabolism appearing early - patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile candidate vector-65 (cachexia). Drift check: `SELECT p.id, p.acronym FROM project p WHERE p.objective ILIKE '%cachexia%' OR p.title ILIKE '%cachexia%'` -> 4 rows (683658 LIFEOMEGA, 741888 CSI-Fun, 897735 REBOOST, 949017 StopWaste), matching the candidate. Read all four: 949017 IN (cachexia is the whole project - futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, ceramides, PDK4); 741888 IN (Cancer associated Cachexia is one of its three named research strands, with mechanism findings on inflammation, the beta-adrenergic system and the sympathetic nervous system); 683658 LIFEOMEGA OUT (an omega-3 EPA food-supplement feasibility study; cachexia named only as a target market for clinical nutrition, no investigation of what drives wasting); 897735 REBOOST OUT (SEPN1-related myopathy; cancer cachexia named once as a condition the model paradigm might later extend to). The gold boundary is drawn on what the question asks - the drivers of the wasting of ADIPOSE TISSUE and MUSCLE - not on whether a project mentions or even works on cachexia. Pooled adjudications on the 19-project pool for the final question text: 818943 UreaCa OUT, and this is the closest call, so the ground is stated exactly. UreaCa's cachexia work is NOT incidental - it is a headline outcome of the project: finalResults report that 're-expressing HNF4a restricted tumor growth and the development of cachexia manifestations' and that 'our results, supported by ERC-PoC, led to a patent and the establishment of a new company - Metabocure, which will evaluate the potential benefit of mRNA of HNF4a delivered via lipid nanoparticles in alleviating cancer cachexia in mice and human'. It is excluded because across its ENTIRE stored text (objective, summary, workPerformed, finalResults, teaser) UreaCa speaks only of whole-organism 'cachexia manifestations' and 'cachexia symptoms' and never localises its HNF4a / liver-metabolism driver to adipose tissue or muscle, which is the tissue-level account this question asks for; a re-deriver who reads the finalResults should therefore not be surprised into reopening the boundary. 677006 CMIL OUT on the cancer/infection split, not on topical absence: CMIL does study cachexia in adipose and muscle tissue ('we became interested into systemic immunometabolic changes and took a particular focus on adipose and muscle tissue'), but the cachexia it experimentally drives and models is infection-associated - 'T cell responses mediate cachexia during viral infection and established a novel model to study infection-associated cachexia' - whereas the question asks about cancer patients. 639548 STARS OUT - thyroid-hormone-driven skeletal muscle wasting across chronic diseases, muscle only, not adipose and not cachexia-targeted; 101033310 Myo_LysoZOOM OUT - lysosomal signalling in muscle wasting generally; 694677 VitruVius OUT - Drosophila growth coordination, host tissue wasting only noted as 'similar to' cancer-induced cachexia; 787041 LIPOMET OUT - lists cancer-associated cachexia as an open future question, no findings; 101003153 FAT-BC, 101020641 PancObese, 748944 LiSDMA, 852086 AGEMEC, 894001 Pept-AGE, 678732 PROMISS, 639382 aCROBAT, 674760 platinDx, 852761 ONco-Energetics_OFF, 964264 TRANSCAN-3, 715575 Reg-Seq, 874708 TheraLymph all OUT on their best chunk (obesity/adiposity, diabetes, sarcopenia, senior malnutrition, brown fat, chemotherapy prediction, tumour bioenergetics, funding coordination, T2D genomics, lymphedema - none about cachexia). Completeness sweep, three non-embedding queries: (a) objective/title ILIKE cachexia|cachectic|wasting syndrome|muscle wasting|tumour-induced weight loss -> 12 projects, (b) report_text summary/workPerformed/finalResults/teaser ILIKE cachexia|cachectic -> 7 projects (639548, 677006, 694677, 741888, 787041, 818943, 949017), (c) cancer/tumour objectives crossed with weight loss|body wasting|adipose tissue loss|fat loss|lean body mass|muscle atrophy or report wasting-of-muscle phrases -> 6 projects, of which 679173 FAT NKT (iNKT cells and obesity), 749978 MATESI (dysphagia) and 814638 GDS (a non-surgical weight-loss sleeve for obesity) were unseen and all read OUT. Every hit across the three sweeps was adjudicated; no satisfying project outside gold. The independent critic's corpus-exhaustive regexp over objective||title||summary||workPerformed||finalResults||teaser for 'cachex|cachect' returned exactly 9 projects corpus-wide, every one of them already adjudicated here, which closes the gold set. term_style exact-term: the question reuses 'cachexia', 'wasting', 'adipose tissue' and 'muscle', all verbatim in both gold texts, and both gold projects are found by lexical (ranks 1 and 4), which is consistent with real term overlap.

evidence:
Gold 741888 CSI-Fun - "Chronic Systemic Inflammation: Functional organ cross-talk in inflammatory disease and cancer". Objective: "The aim of this research proposal is to substantially advance our understanding of whole organ physiology in relation to systemic inflammation as a cause or/and consequence of disease with the focus on Psoriasis/Joint Diseases and Cancer Cachexia. ... such as Inflammatory Skin/Joint disease and Cachexia, a deadly systemic manifestation of Cancer." Report summary: "3. Cancer associated Cachexia (CAC): is a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients, characterized by involuntary loss of body weight due to wasting of muscles and fat. CAC is detrimental to cancer patients' quality of life and considered the immediate cause of death for a third of of cancer patients. ... We studied how uncontrolled inflammation, perturbed hormone balance and the nervous system operate and interact during CAC using model systems that mimic the patient situation. We experimentally demonstrated that inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players that should be closely monitored in patients. In addition, we showed how immune cells interact with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC".

Gold 949017 StopWaste - "Targeting the crosstalk of lipid and glucose metabolism to stop cancer-associated wasting". Objective: "Cachexia is the deadly outcome of many late stage cancers. It is characterized by severe wasting of adipose tissue and muscle mass, cardiac dysfunction and systemic inflammation. ... My current data support the new concept that tumors activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, which leads to an energy crisis that drives systemic metabolic dysfunction. ... perturbed adipose tissue in cachexia causes the increased release of bioreactive signaling lipids such as C16:0 ceramides which appear before any wasting occurs." Report summary: "We have identified bioreactive lipid species specific to cachexia that result from alterations in liver lipids and dysregulation of key enzymes of liver lipid metabolism. We found that these lipids contributed to cachexia by influencing muscle and liver metabolism, and could be targeted using the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin. ... we identified substantial differences between cachectic and non-cachectic adipose tissue, particularly an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA). Dysfunctional adipose tissue metabolism was partially linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. ... patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers".

Discrimination counter-examples (the four nearest rejects, all pooled top-10 in at least one condition):
- 677006 CMIL, lexical rank 2 - workPerformed: "We uncovered a previously unrecognized role by our T cell responses mediate cachexia during viral infection and established a novel model to study infection-associated cachexia (Baazim et al. 2019)". Its cachexia is infection-driven, not tumour-driven. OUT.
- 818943 UreaCa, hybrid rank 7 - workPerformed: "we demonstrate that liver metabolism is affected by extrahepatic cancers leading to systemic changes and promoting cancer progression to cachexia." One downstream result of a urea-cycle-in-carcinogenesis project, not a study of what drives the wasting. OUT.
- 639548 STARS, lexical rank 3 - objective: "Skeletal muscle wasting is a devastating complication of many chronic diseases including cancer, diabetes, chronic heart failure and cystic fibrosis." Muscle only, thyroid-hormone therapy angle, not cachexia-targeted and silent on adipose. OUT.
- 694677 VitruVius, hybrid_rerank rank 5 - workPerformed: "We have identified a hormone sequestration mechanism linking tumor growth and host tissue wasting, similar to what is observed during cancer-induced cachexia". Drosophila body-size work; the cachexia link is an analogy. OUT.

Seed rejects from the candidate's own four: 683658 LIFEOMEGA objective - "most of cancer patients suffer cachexia or anorexia. EPA supports weight management" (a food-supplement feasibility and business study). 897735 REBOOST objective - "other inherited or acquired myopathies sharing an underlying bioenergetic deficiency, including sarcopenia and cancer cachexia" (SEPN1-related myopathy).

why_good: This question discriminates on whether a system can tell a project that investigates cancer cachexia from the much larger set that merely names it - the corpus has nine projects whose text contains "cachexia", and six of them rank in the pooled top-10 while satisfying nothing. It fills the medical-and-health-sciences / clinical-medicine bucket on the vector L2 synthesis cell with an exact-term topic, an axis the bank has not covered. The L2 label is arithmetic, not asserted: exactly two projects study what drives the wasting, and the synthesis label is honest because neither gold project alone gives the account - CSI-Fun supplies the inflammatory and neuro-endocrine drivers and StopWaste the lipid-glucose metabolic ones, and the answer has to fuse them rather than contrast them.

findings.ruling_why: Upheld in round 1, fix ordered and delivered; the critic re-attacked and did not re-raise it, so the class is settled on this candidate and is not re-ruled.

The critic's full read of 741888 is correct that the boundary sentence, worded as a property of where the driver is localised, would exclude gold member CSI-Fun too, so the recorded reason does not cleanly re-derive the gold set. It is real and rides into the report as a note, because the gold set, level, subtype, term_style, reference and question text are all independently confirmed sound and the defect lives entirely in one sentence of internal justification.

judge_decisions.rationale: The question measures whether a vector condition pools 741888 and 949017 and synthesizes the drivers of adipose and muscle wasting, and every load-bearing part of that now has two independent executions behind it: the critic re-ran the pooled retrieval itself and reproduced the rank matrix byte-for-byte, its fresh own-wording draw returned both golds and no new satisfying project, and its corpus-exhaustive sweep closes the gold set at 2. The round-2 finding does not touch any of that - it says the notes state the UreaCa exclusion in terms of driver localisation when the contrast that actually holds is what each project names as the phenomenon it explains, and the critic supplies that better line itself. That is a defect in the recorded reason, not in what is measured, and the drafter's one fix round is spent. Abandoning a question whose gold, level, cell and retrieval behaviour are all verified, to buy a one-sentence rewording at the price of a fresh candidate and drafter pass, would cost the bank a sound entry to fix a note - so it is accepted with the finding recorded for the user's promote-time veto, where the exact wording is a cheap edit if he wants it.

record.text: Which projects are developing ways to pull the plant nutrients out of livestock slurry and dung and concentrate them into a fertiliser product that can be stored and handled like a bought fertiliser, instead of the raw waste simply being spread on nearby fields?
record.reference_answer: Twelve projects treat livestock manure or slurry as a raw material and pull its nitrogen and phosphorus into a fertiliser that can be stored, moved and sold, rather than spread raw under the EU Nitrates Directive limits. Separation and drying routes: UltraBio splits manure and digestate with ultrasound so most nutrients bind to a solid product that is pelletised and sold as a storable organic fertiliser while the liquid can be released; ENFIR dehydrates manure with far-infrared heat into pelletized compost, producing more than 1.500 ton/year of organic fertilizer per unit; IMBIO processes animal waste including chicken manure into organic fertilizers for small and medium farms. Nitrogen-capture routes: Poul-AR biologically converts poultry manure's organic nitrogen to ammonia, strips it with air and fixes it with sulphuric or nitric acid as an ammonium salt fertilizer; AMBIENCE captures 70% - 80% of the ammonia from pig farms and biogas plant digestate with permeable membranes and delivers Ammonia Sulphate (NH4)2SO4 for fertilizer manufacturers. Whole-plant recovery: FERTIMANURE runs 5 on-farm pilots and targets 31 marketable end-products; DEPURGAN's electrocoagulation reactor yields a solid fraction with calorific potential plus an NPK liquid effluent; SYSTEMIC processes digestate of pig manure into a mineral N fertiliser, an organic soil improver and a P fertiliser, explicitly to reduce the import of P as a finite resource from mines. Manure is one feedstock among several in NewFert (ashes of different origins and livestock effluents into a new generation of fertilisers) and B-FERST (struvite from pig slurries, plus ashes and compost, into 8 specialised fertilisers). VALI and SUSTAINABLEFARM pair energy recovery with a fertiliser product - VALI burns manure for heat and electricity leaving compact, easy-to-transport ashes directly usable as dry fertilizer, and SUSTAINABLEFARM converts manure into biogas and organic fertilizers.

record.text: Several projects set out to uncover how animals tell direction from the planet's magnetic field. How do these projects differ in the animal each chose to work with and in the physical explanation each set out to test?
record.reference_answer: The four projects split by study animal and by which proposed physical mechanism they set out to test. QuantumBirds works on night-migratory songbirds and set out to prove whether detection happens in the retina through the quantum spin dynamics of photochemically formed radical pairs in cryptochrome proteins. MagneticMoth uses the Australian Bogong moth, aiming to decide between the two contending hypotheses and targeting photoreceptor-based cryptochrome (Cry) molecules in the eyes, having cloned genes for 4 visual opsins and 2 Cry. NeuroMag uses pigeons as a model system and asks whether the primary sensors are inner ear hair cells and whether detection depends on magnetic crystals (magnetite) or on electromagnetic induction, while NeuroMagMa takes mole-rats, a rodent living in darkness underground, and pursues the magnetite theory plus magnetic input to head direction cells.

record.text: Which projects are developing ways to pull the plant nutrients out of livestock slurry and dung and concentrate them into a fertiliser product that can be stored and handled like a bought fertiliser, instead of the raw waste simply being spread on nearby fields?
record.reference_answer: Thirteen projects treat livestock manure or slurry as a raw material and pull its nitrogen and phosphorus into a fertiliser that can be stored, moved and sold, rather than spread raw under the EU Nitrates Directive limits. Separation and drying routes: UltraBio splits manure and digestate with ultrasound so most nutrients bind to a solid product that is pelletised and sold as a storable organic fertiliser while the liquid can be released; ENFIR dehydrates manure with far-infrared heat into pelletized compost, producing more than 1.500 ton/year of organic fertilizer per unit; IMBIO processes animal waste including chicken manure into organic fertilizers for small and medium farms. Nitrogen-capture routes: Poul-AR biologically converts poultry manure's organic nitrogen to ammonia, strips it with air and fixes it with sulphuric or nitric acid as an ammonium salt fertilizer; AMBIENCE captures 70% - 80% of the ammonia from pig farms and biogas plant digestate with permeable membranes and delivers Ammonia Sulphate (NH4)2SO4 for fertilizer manufacturers; ADD-ON's Ductor process removes over 60% of the nitrogen from high-nitrogen organic waste such as chicken manure before biogasification and sells the recovered nitrogen on, having met 'potential equipment suppliers and potential off-takers for ammonium sulphate'. Whole-plant recovery: FERTIMANURE runs 5 on-farm pilots and targets 31 marketable end-products; DEPURGAN's electrocoagulation reactor yields a solid fraction with calorific potential plus an NPK liquid effluent; SYSTEMIC processes digestate of pig manure into a mineral N fertiliser, an organic soil improver and a P fertiliser, explicitly to reduce the import of P as a finite resource from mines; Circular Agronomics developed five technologies (solar drying, microfiltration and fertigation, vacuum degasification, k-struvite recovery, membrane treatment) that yielded 'up to 6 bio-based products compiling the new European Fertilizing Regulation or struvite application requirements', keeping 'up to 62% of N from manure digestate ... in the fertilizer product in a more stable form', with 'a new solar drying system to produce bio-based fertilizers'. Manure is one feedstock among several in NewFert (ashes of different origins and livestock effluents into a new generation of fertilisers) and B-FERST (struvite from pig slurries, plus ashes and compost, into 8 specialised fertilisers). VALI pairs energy recovery with a fertiliser product, burning manure for heat and electricity and leaving compact, easy-to-transport ashes directly usable as dry fertilizer.
