why_good: The question asks in plain user words ('slurry and dung', 'plant nutrients', 'stored and handled like a bought fertiliser') for a family the corpus names as 'nutrient recovery', 'valorisation', 'digestate', 'struvite' and 'bio-based fertiliser', so no single condition's top-15 finds it: 7 of the 13 gold projects sit outside every condition's k=15. It discriminates on a bright line inside a crowded neighbourhood - projects that only improve manure in place (GasAbate N+, NITROBIO, Sustainable Manure, SUSTAINABLEFARM) rank highly and are wrong, while the ones that separate a saleable product (Poul-AR, ENFIR, IMBIO, AMBIENCE, ADD-ON, VALI, Circular Agronomics) are largely invisible. L3 is honest by definition: 13 gold projects.

findings.ruling_why: The critic's full read of 773649 Circular Agronomics shows nutrient recovery from manure digestate and dairy slurry into regulation-compliant fertiliser products, which is the same admission channel the drafter used for SYSTEMIC, and the mixed-feedstock objection cannot separate it from NewFert and B-FERST which are already IN on mixed feedstock.

The critic's read of 957068 SUSTAINABLEFARM's report shows the nutrients remain in the digestate which is pasteurised and pumped onto the farm's own fields, which is precisely the case the question's closing clause excludes, and the drafter's only counter-evidence is an objective-line marketing phrase of the kind it itself rejected for ADFU, NOMAD, biowave and GASFARM.

666427 ADD-ON strips over 60% of nitrogen from chicken litter and takes it to off-takers as ammonium sulphate, the same process and output the drafter admitted AMBIENCE on, so leaving it unadjudicated in either direction means the gold set's boundary is not re-derivable by an independent reader; 727874 SABANA is weaker but is equally unrecorded.

The brief only requires that the rank matrix not contradict the declared style, and 5 of 12 gold sitting outside every condition's top 15 (reproduced in the critic's own run) keeps paraphrase defensible even though lexical reaches 6 of 12 at k=15; this rides into the report as a note with the critic's rank list, and is never re-ruled on this candidate.

judge_decisions.rationale: The cell is a vector L3 survey, so the measurement is exactly 'does the condition find the whole set of manure-to-fertiliser-product projects' - an incomplete gold set punishes the system that found Circular Agronomics, and a gold member whose nutrients go straight back onto the fields rewards a system that ignored the question's own exclusion clause. Both defects are the brief's second failure mode and both have a bounded fix that leaves the question, the scope statement and the paraphrase argument untouched. After the fix |gold| lands at 12 or 13, comfortably inside vector L3, so the slot does not move cell.

record.text: Several EU-funded projects are working towards next-generation optical and nuclear clocks. For the ones whose clock work is centred on one specific named element, isotope or ion species, which projects are they and which species is each clock referenced to?
record.reference_answer: Nine projects centre their clock work on a named reference species, in three families. Strontium dominates the neutral-atom optical clocks: Mobiclock develops a mobile optical lattice clock on strontium atoms, iqClock's prototype is a field-ready strontium optical clock, and Q-Sense's space optical clock demonstrator (SOC2) is based on cold Sr atoms; TICTOCGRAV pursues optical clocks on both cadmium and strontium. A second family replaces the electron-shell transition with the low-energy nuclear isomer of Thorium-229: nuClock, ThoriumNuclearClock, CRYSTALCLOCK (a readout scheme for a solid-state 229Th clock) and RaDTho (measuring that isomer's radiative decay towards a nuclear frequency standard). FunClocks stands apart by referencing optical clocks to highly charged ions - it operated an Ar13+ clock and performs isotope-shift spectroscopy on highly charged calcium ions.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 seed vector-56 (9 projects whose objective/title contains 'optical clock'); the question was composed after reading their text. Membership test, stated in the question and applied identically to every project: the project's own text ties its clock work to one named element, isotope or ion species. The test is about what the clock is referenced TO, never about how far the project got, so plans and completed work are treated alike. record.text: Several projects set out to uncover how animals tell direction from the planet's magnetic field. How do these projects differ in the animal each chose to work with and in the physical explanation each set out to test?
record.reference_answer: The four projects split by study animal and by which proposed physical mechanism they set out to test. QuantumBirds works on night-migratory songbirds and set out to prove whether detection happens in the retina through the quantum spin dynamics of photochemically formed radical pairs in cryptochrome proteins. MagneticMoth uses the Australian Bogong moth, aiming to decide between the two contending hypotheses and targeting photoreceptor-based cryptochrome (Cry) molecules in the eyes, having cloned genes for 4 visual opsins and 2 Cry. NeuroMag uses pigeons as a model system and asks whether the primary sensors are inner ear hair cells and whether detection depends on magnetic crystals (magnetite) or on electromagnetic induction, while NeuroMagMa takes mole-rats, a rodent living in darkness underground, and pursues the magnetite theory plus magnetic input to head direction cells.

why_good: The question forces a system to separate animal magnetic-sensing biology from the far larger population of planetary and stellar magnetic-field projects that dominate lexical retrieval on the same words - lexical's top ten contains one gold project, dense's contains three. It fills a sensory-biology axis the bank does not yet touch and a paraphrase cell: the question uses none of the projects' headline vocabulary (magnetoreception, magnetic sense, compass, cryptochrome, magnetite), and three of four gold projects are unreachable lexically. The L2 comparison label is honest because |gold| = 4 after a 48-row non-embedding sweep found no fifth satisfying project, and the four texts differ sharply on both compared dimensions - moth/songbird/pigeon/mole-rat, and cryptochrome radical pairs vs magnetite vs electromagnetic induction.

findings.claim: The second comparison dimension is worded as one mechanism per project, while 819336 and 741298 each set out to discriminate between two competing mechanisms. A solver can defensibly answer with a single mechanism per project ('NeuroMag: magnetite') or with the pair ('magnetite versus electromagnetic induction'), and the two answers differ in content while both being faithful to the text.
findings.evidence: 819336 NeuroMag objective, read in full: 'In Aim 1 we will explore whether inner ear hair cells are the primary sensors, and if the detection of magnetic stimuli depends on the presence of magnetic crystals or electromagnetic induction' - and its report summary lists three candidate ideas (light-sensitive quantal model; iron-based compass; electromagnetic induction). 741298 MagneticMoth objective: 'isolating which of the two current (contentious) hypotheses for magnetic sensation apply. The most likely of these involves ... photoreceptor-based cryptochrome (Cry) molecules in the eyes'. By contrast 810002 and 948728 do name one mechanism each (radical pairs in cryptochrome; magnetite). The reference answer already covers the pair form for both, so the losing reading is the singular one - the mismatch is with the question's wording, not with the gold set.
findings.fix_direction: Reword the second dimension in the plural-tolerant form, e.g. '...and in the physical mechanism or mechanisms each set out to test'. No change to gold, level or subtype.

record.text: Several EU-funded projects are working towards next-generation optical and nuclear clocks. For the ones whose clock work is centred on one specific named element, isotope or ion species, which projects are they and which species is each clock referenced to?
record.reference_answer: Nine projects centre their clock work on a named reference species, in three families. Strontium dominates the neutral-atom optical clocks: Mobiclock develops a mobile optical lattice clock on strontium atoms, iqClock's prototype is a field-ready strontium optical clock, and Q-Sense's space optical clock demonstrator (SOC2) is based on cold Sr atoms; TICTOCGRAV pursues optical clocks on both cadmium and strontium. A second family replaces the electron-shell transition with the low-energy nuclear isomer of Thorium-229: nuClock, ThoriumNuclearClock, CRYSTALCLOCK (a readout scheme for a solid-state 229Th clock) and RaDTho (measuring that isomer's radiative decay towards a nuclear frequency standard). FunClocks stands apart by referencing optical clocks to highly charged ions - it operated an Ar13+ clock and performs isotope-shift spectroscopy on highly charged calcium ions.

findings.claim: The membership criterion says the clock work must be centred on ONE SPECIFIC named element, isotope or ion species. Two gold members fail that literal reading: TICTOCGRAV is built on two species, and FunClocks' clock reference is a class of ions, not a species. A reader applying the wording as written returns 7 projects; the drafter's gold is 9. Both readings are defensible and they answer differently.
findings.evidence: 772126 TICTOCGRAV, own title and report: 'Exploring Gravity with Ultracold Cadmium and Strontium Optical Clocks and Bragg Interferometers' / 'a novel dual-species atom interferometer based on optical clock transitions of ultra-cold cadmium (Cd) and strontium (Sr) atoms' - explicitly dual-species. 101019987 FunClocks, own title 'Testing Fundamental Physics with Highly Charged Ion Clocks' and report summary 'Precision spectroscopy of highly charged ions (HCI) provides insight into atomic systems' - the reference is the HCI class; Ar13+ is one demonstration and the calcium work is isotope-shift spectroscopy, not the clock's reference species. findings.fix_direction: Drop the numeral from the criterion and let the answer carry the multiplicity - e.g. '...whose clock work is referenced to a specifically named element, isotope or ion species (one or more)... which species is each clock referenced to?' record.text: Several projects set out to uncover how animals tell direction from the planet's magnetic field. How do these projects differ in the animal each chose to work with and in which candidate physical mechanism or mechanisms each set out to weigh up?
record.reference_answer: The four projects split by study animal and by which proposed physical mechanism they set out to test. QuantumBirds works on night-migratory songbirds and set out to prove whether detection happens in the retina through the quantum spin dynamics of photochemically formed radical pairs in cryptochrome proteins. MagneticMoth uses the Australian Bogong moth, aiming to decide between the two contending hypotheses and targeting photoreceptor-based cryptochrome (Cry) molecules in the eyes, having cloned genes for 4 visual opsins and 2 Cry. NeuroMag uses pigeons as a model system and asks whether the primary sensors are inner ear hair cells and whether detection depends on magnetic crystals (magnetite) or on electromagnetic induction, while NeuroMagMa takes mole-rats, a rodent living in darkness underground, and pursues the magnetite theory plus magnetic input to head direction cells.

FIX ROUND 1 reworded the second comparison dimension from 'the physical explanation each set out to test' (singular) to 'which candidate physical mechanism or mechanisms each set out to weigh up', because 819336 ('whether ... magnetic crystals or electromagnetic induction', three candidate ideas in its report summary) and 741298 ('isolating which of the two current (contentious) hypotheses ... apply') set out to adjudicate between mechanisms rather than test one; naming one mechanism for 810002/948728 and two for 819336/741298 is now equally admissible. record.text: Several EU-funded projects are working towards next-generation optical and nuclear clocks. For the ones whose clock work is centred on one specific named element, isotope or ion species, which projects are they and which species is each clock referenced to?
record.reference_answer: Nine projects centre their clock work on a named reference species, in three families. Strontium dominates the neutral-atom optical clocks: Mobiclock develops a mobile optical lattice clock on strontium atoms, iqClock's prototype is a field-ready strontium optical clock, and Q-Sense's space optical clock demonstrator (SOC2) is based on cold Sr atoms; TICTOCGRAV pursues optical clocks on both cadmium and strontium. A second family replaces the electron-shell transition with the low-energy nuclear isomer of Thorium-229: nuClock, ThoriumNuclearClock, CRYSTALCLOCK (a readout scheme for a solid-state 229Th clock) and RaDTho (measuring that isomer's radiative decay towards a nuclear frequency standard). FunClocks stands apart by referencing optical clocks to highly charged ions - it operated an Ar13+ clock and performs isotope-shift spectroscopy on highly charged calcium ions.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 seed vector-56 (9 projects whose objective/title contains 'optical clock'); the question was composed after reading their text. Membership test, stated in the question and applied identically to every project: the project's own text ties its clock work to one named element, isotope or ion species. The test is about what the clock is referenced TO, never about how far the project got, so plans and completed work are treated alike. findings.ruling_why: The critic's executed reads support it: TICTOCGRAV's own title and report describe a dual-species Cd+Sr optical clock and FunClocks' own title and summary reference the highly-charged-ion class, so the literal criterion 'centred on ONE SPECIFIC named element, isotope or ion species' returns 7 while the recorded gold is 9 - two defensible readings that answer differently, which the brief calls HIGH; the draft's own reference answer concedes the FunClocks point in writing.

judge_decisions.rationale: The cell is sound and the gold is sound; only the counting word in the criterion is wrong, and it moves the scored answer set from 9 to 7, which is exactly the 'measures the wrong thing' failure - a system that correctly returns TICTOCGRAV and FunClocks would be marked down under the reader's reading. This is not candidate 0's defect recurring: that one was a maturity ambiguity (built vs actually demonstrated) reaching into whether a project's work counted at all, and this drafter closed it explicitly in the membership test, which the critic did not attack; the live ambiguity is about how many species a member may name, a different axis. Candidate 0's disposition also keyed on GOLD-WRONG, so AMBIGUOUS-READING has killed one candidate, not two, and the cross-candidate stop rule does not fire. The fix is bounded to the criterion's wording with the gold set and the pooling evidence untouched, so one fix round should land it.

record.text: Which projects are developing ways to pull the plant nutrients out of livestock slurry and dung and concentrate them into a fertiliser product that can be stored and handled like a bought fertiliser, instead of the raw waste simply being spread on nearby fields?
record.reference_answer: Thirteen projects treat livestock manure or slurry as a raw material and pull its nitrogen and phosphorus into a fertiliser that can be stored, moved and sold, rather than spread raw under the EU Nitrates Directive limits. Separation and drying routes: UltraBio splits manure and digestate with ultrasound so most nutrients bind to a solid product that is pelletised and sold as a storable organic fertiliser while the liquid can be released; ENFIR dehydrates manure with far-infrared heat into pelletized compost, producing more than 1.500 ton/year of organic fertilizer per unit; IMBIO processes animal waste including chicken manure into organic fertilizers for small and medium farms. Nitrogen-capture routes: Poul-AR biologically converts poultry manure's organic nitrogen to ammonia, strips it with air and fixes it with sulphuric or nitric acid as an ammonium salt fertilizer; AMBIENCE captures 70% - 80% of the ammonia from pig farms and biogas plant digestate with permeable membranes and delivers Ammonia Sulphate (NH4)2SO4 for fertilizer manufacturers; ADD-ON's Ductor process removes over 60% of the nitrogen from high-nitrogen organic waste such as chicken manure before biogasification and sells the recovered nitrogen on, having met 'potential equipment suppliers and potential off-takers for ammonium sulphate'. Whole-plant recovery: FERTIMANURE runs 5 on-farm pilots and targets 31 marketable end-products; DEPURGAN's electrocoagulation reactor yields a solid fraction with calorific potential plus an NPK liquid effluent; SYSTEMIC processes digestate of pig manure into a mineral N fertiliser, an organic soil improver and a P fertiliser, explicitly to reduce the import of P as a finite resource from mines; Circular Agronomics developed five technologies (solar drying, microfiltration and fertigation, vacuum degasification, k-struvite recovery, membrane treatment) that yielded 'up to 6 bio-based products compiling the new European Fertilizing Regulation or struvite application requirements', keeping 'up to 62% of N from manure digestate ... in the fertilizer product in a more stable form', with 'a new solar drying system to produce bio-based fertilizers'. Manure is one feedstock among several in NewFert (ashes of different origins and livestock effluents into a new generation of fertilisers) and B-FERST (struvite from pig slurries, plus ashes and compost, into 8 specialised fertilisers). VALI pairs energy recovery with a fertiliser product, burning manure for heat and electricity and leaving compact, easy-to-transport ashes directly usable as dry fertilizer.

findings.claim: 854814 ADFU concentrates AD liquor nutrients onto solids as a granular, storable, transportable fertiliser and frames itself exactly against raw spreading. It is weaker than NOMAD only because its objective never names livestock manure.
findings.evidence: run_sql full objective for 854814: 'Digestate is commonly used as a raw liquid fertiliser on land, with associated problems of run-off, leaching ... We have developed novel methods to convert the waste liquor from AD into a low cost, granular fertiliser. The contained liquor nutrients are concentrated onto readily available solids to higher levels which can be stored and transported easily, and later used as a fertiliser.' finalResults: 'nutrient absorption and fertiliser granulation can occur in the same process using a variety of feedstocks', the device 'initially intended for use in the farm waste AD sector'. That sentence pair is a near-restatement of the question's own criterion. The only exclusion ground left is feedstock provenance, which F3 shows the record does not apply consistently.

record.text: Several projects set out to uncover how animals tell direction from the planet's magnetic field. How do these projects differ in the animal each chose to work with and in which candidate physical mechanism or mechanisms each set out to weigh up?
record.reference_answer: The four projects split by study animal and by which proposed physical mechanism they set out to test. QuantumBirds works on night-migratory songbirds and set out to prove whether detection happens in the retina through the quantum spin dynamics of photochemically formed radical pairs in cryptochrome proteins. MagneticMoth uses the Australian Bogong moth, aiming to decide between the two contending hypotheses and targeting photoreceptor-based cryptochrome (Cry) molecules in the eyes, having cloned genes for 4 visual opsins and 2 Cry. NeuroMag uses pigeons as a model system and asks whether the primary sensors are inner ear hair cells and whether detection depends on magnetic crystals (magnetite) or on electromagnetic induction, while NeuroMagMa takes mole-rats, a rodent living in darkness underground, and pursues the magnetite theory plus magnetic input to head direction cells.

record.text: Several EU-funded projects are working towards next-generation optical and nuclear clocks. For the ones whose clock work is referenced to a specifically named element, isotope or ion species (one or more), which projects are they and which species is each clock referenced to?
record.reference_answer: Nine projects tie their clock work to named reference species, in three families. Strontium dominates the neutral-atom optical clocks: Mobiclock develops a mobile optical lattice clock on strontium atoms, iqClock's prototype is a field-ready strontium optical clock, and Q-Sense's space optical clock demonstrator (SOC2) is based on cold Sr atoms; TICTOCGRAV works on optical clocks referenced to two species, ultra-cold cadmium (Cd) and strontium (Sr). A second family replaces the electron-shell transition with the low-energy nuclear isomer of Thorium-229: nuClock, ThoriumNuclearClock, CRYSTALCLOCK (a readout scheme for a solid-state 229Th clock) and RaDTho (measuring that isomer's radiative decay towards a nuclear frequency standard). FunClocks references its optical clocks to highly charged ions, naming Ar13+, on which it operated a clock, and highly charged calcium ions used for isotope-shift spectroscopy.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 seed vector-56 (9 projects whose objective/title contains 'optical clock'); the question was composed after reading their text. Membership test, stated in the question and applied identically to every project: the project's own text ties its clock work to at least one named element, isotope or ion species. Naming a species is the test; the NUMBER of species is not - a project referencing one species and a project referencing two are both in, and the answer field carries the multiplicity. The test is also about what the clock is referenced TO, never about how far the project got, so plans, components and completed work are treated alike. IN: 707864 Mobiclock (strontium optical lattice clock); 820404 iqClock (field-ready strontium optical clock); 772126 TICTOCGRAV (cadmium AND strontium optical clocks - two named species); 691156 Q-Sense (report workPerformed: 'Space Optical Clock (SOC2): It is based on cold Sr atoms'); 856415 ThoriumNuclearClock (Th-229 isomer); 664732 nuClock (clock based on a nuclear transition in Thorium-229); 882708 CRYSTALCLOCK (readout for a solid-state 229Th nuclear clock); 101026762 RaDTho (thorium-229 isomer characterisation towards a nuclear clock/frequency standard); 101019987 FunClocks (highly charged ions, naming Ar13+ and highly charged calcium ions). OUT with reasons - every one names NO species tied to a clock, or no clock: 757386 quMercury - laser cooling and isotope-shift spectroscopy of Hg-199 for an EDM measurement, with Hg lattice clocks named only as a downstream beneficiary of its technologies; 860579 MoSaiQC - builds portable and superradiant clock modules but names no element, isotope or ion species anywhere in its own prose (strontium-88 appears only inside listed publication titles); 820393 macQsimal - workPerformed names 'the miniature atomic clock' but no species; 795121 photonicIons - applied atomic spectroscopy on trapped ytterbium and calcium ions to search for a fifth fundamental force, named species but no clock; 965124 FEMTOCHIP - chip-scale femtosecond laser enabling clocks, no species; 851758 TeLSCombe, 853522 REFOCUS, 727493 ULTRASTABLE - frequency combs, no clock species; 731107 CLONETS, 951886 CLONETS-DS - clock distribution networks, no species; 801285 PIEDMONS, 699387 NAVISAS, 750017 QUESCA, 648575 LIVIN, 949119 CoMoFun - clocks named only as an application of ion traps/cold atoms/molecules, no clock of their own; 832219 ANDLICA, 661171 SYMULGAS, 682629 TOPSIM, 803047 LaGaTYb - ultracold Sr/Yb quantum-simulation projects that name a species and mention clocks only as motivation; 742247 XUV-COMB, 670168 NEWPHYS-MOLECULES - precision spectroscopy of He+/H2, not a clock; remaining pooled hits (714118 TRAPLAB, 695618 Photonis, 844829 RAPTOR, 824096 RADIATE, 861198 LISA, 661777 MagicTin, 818744 INITIUM, 864792 OXYGEN, 892383 RESCATA) are off-topic trap/isotope/geoscience work. findings.ruling_why: The critic's executed reads support it: TICTOCGRAV's own title and report describe a dual-species Cd+Sr optical clock and FunClocks' own title and summary reference the highly-charged-ion class, so the literal criterion 'centred on ONE SPECIFIC named element, isotope or ion species' returns 7 while the recorded gold is 9 - two defensible readings that answer differently, which the brief calls HIGH; the draft's own reference answer concedes the FunClocks point in writing.

judge_decisions.rationale: The cell is sound and the gold is sound; only the counting word in the criterion is wrong, and it moves the scored answer set from 9 to 7, which is exactly the 'measures the wrong thing' failure - a system that correctly returns TICTOCGRAV and FunClocks would be marked down under the reader's reading. This is not candidate 0's defect recurring: that one was a maturity ambiguity (built vs actually demonstrated) reaching into whether a project's work counted at all, and this drafter closed it explicitly in the membership test, which the critic did not attack; the live ambiguity is about how many species a member may name, a different axis. Candidate 0's disposition also keyed on GOLD-WRONG, so AMBIGUOUS-READING has killed one candidate, not two, and the cross-candidate stop rule does not fire. The fix is bounded to the criterion's wording with the gold set and the pooling evidence untouched, so one fix round should land it.

record.text: Several projects set out to uncover how animals tell direction from the planet's magnetic field. How do these projects differ in the animal each chose to work with and in which candidate physical mechanism or mechanisms each set out to weigh up?
record.reference_answer: The four projects split by study animal and by which proposed physical mechanism they set out to test. QuantumBirds works on night-migratory songbirds and set out to prove whether detection happens in the retina through the quantum spin dynamics of photochemically formed radical pairs in cryptochrome proteins. MagneticMoth uses the Australian Bogong moth, aiming to decide between the two contending hypotheses and targeting photoreceptor-based cryptochrome (Cry) molecules in the eyes, having cloned genes for 4 visual opsins and 2 Cry. NeuroMag uses pigeons as a model system and asks whether the primary sensors are inner ear hair cells and whether detection depends on magnetic crystals (magnetite) or on electromagnetic induction, while NeuroMagMa takes mole-rats, a rodent living in darkness underground, and pursues the magnetite theory plus magnetic input to head direction cells.

record.text: Several EU-funded projects are working towards next-generation optical and nuclear clocks. For the ones whose clock work is referenced to a specifically named element, isotope or ion species (one or more), which projects are they and which species is each clock referenced to?
record.reference_answer: Nine projects tie their clock work to named reference species, in three families. Strontium dominates the neutral-atom optical clocks: Mobiclock develops a mobile optical lattice clock on strontium atoms, iqClock's prototype is a field-ready strontium optical clock, and Q-Sense's space optical clock demonstrator (SOC2) is based on cold Sr atoms; TICTOCGRAV works on optical clocks referenced to two species, ultra-cold cadmium (Cd) and strontium (Sr). A second family replaces the electron-shell transition with the low-energy nuclear isomer of Thorium-229: nuClock, ThoriumNuclearClock, CRYSTALCLOCK (a readout scheme for a solid-state 229Th clock) and RaDTho (measuring that isomer's radiative decay towards a nuclear frequency standard). FunClocks references its optical clocks to highly charged ions, naming Ar13+, on which it operated a clock, and highly charged calcium ions used for isotope-shift spectroscopy.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 seed vector-56 (9 projects whose objective/title contains 'optical clock'); the question was composed after reading their text. Membership test, stated in the question and applied identically to every project: the project's own text ties its clock work to at least one named element, isotope or ion species. Naming a species is the test; the NUMBER of species is not - a project referencing one species and a project referencing two are both in, and the answer field carries the multiplicity. The test is also about what the clock is referenced TO, never about how far the project got, so plans, components and completed work are treated alike. IN: 707864 Mobiclock (strontium optical lattice clock); 820404 iqClock (field-ready strontium optical clock); 772126 TICTOCGRAV (cadmium AND strontium optical clocks - two named species); 691156 Q-Sense (report workPerformed: 'Space Optical Clock (SOC2): It is based on cold Sr atoms'); 856415 ThoriumNuclearClock (Th-229 isomer); 664732 nuClock (clock based on a nuclear transition in Thorium-229); 882708 CRYSTALCLOCK (readout for a solid-state 229Th nuclear clock); 101026762 RaDTho (thorium-229 isomer characterisation towards a nuclear clock/frequency standard); 101019987 FunClocks (highly charged ions, naming Ar13+ and highly charged calcium ions). record.text: Several EU-funded projects are working towards next-generation optical and nuclear clocks. For the ones whose clock work is referenced to a specifically named element, isotope or ion species (one or more), which projects are they and which species is each clock referenced to?
record.reference_answer: Nine projects tie their clock work to named reference species, in three families. Strontium dominates the neutral-atom optical clocks: Mobiclock develops a mobile optical lattice clock on strontium atoms, iqClock's prototype is a field-ready strontium optical clock, and Q-Sense's space optical clock demonstrator (SOC2) is based on cold Sr atoms; TICTOCGRAV works on optical clocks referenced to two species, ultra-cold cadmium (Cd) and strontium (Sr). A second family replaces the electron-shell transition with the low-energy nuclear isomer of Thorium-229: nuClock, ThoriumNuclearClock, CRYSTALCLOCK (a readout scheme for a solid-state 229Th clock) and RaDTho (measuring that isomer's radiative decay towards a nuclear frequency standard). FunClocks references its optical clocks to highly charged ions, naming Ar13+, on which it operated a clock, and highly charged calcium ions used for isotope-shift spectroscopy.
record.notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 seed vector-56 (9 projects whose objective/title contains 'optical clock'); the question was composed after reading their text. Membership test, stated in the question and applied identically to every project: the project's own text ties its clock work to at least one named element, isotope or ion species. Naming a species is the test; the NUMBER of species is not - a project referencing one species and a project referencing two are both in, and the answer field carries the multiplicity. The test is also about what the clock is referenced TO, never about how far the project got, so plans, components and completed work are treated alike. record.text: How do EU-funded research projects go about explaining what decides which role an individual ends up taking inside an insect colony?
record.reference_answer: Seven projects treat the assignment of roles inside an insect society as the thing to be explained, and they attack it at very different levels. Genomic and molecular work dominates: RoyalMess searches for the genes that fate a Messor ant embryo to become a queen or a worker under social hybridogenesis; MELCA uses the double-clonal longhorn crazy ant Paratrechina longicornis to separate the molecular signatures of sex from those of the queen-versus-worker caste; and CASTECON asks whether inter-caste genetic correlations stop queens and workers from each reaching their own optimal dimorphic phenotype, and whether queens manipulate worker phenotype in their own interests. Physiology and neurobiology supply a second angle: DRiveR tests whether dopamine carries the Queen Mandibular Pheromone (QMP) signal that inhibits ovary activity in honeybee workers, while resiliANT measured the lipid content of individual ants by Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and, with targeted starvation, established a causal relationship between fat content and division of labour. MechAnt takes a mechanical view, tying the cutting ability of differently-sized leaf-cutter workers to the ontogeny of task choice and testing whether leaf-cutter colonies are organised according to ergonomic criteria. Division is the broadest: it asks across species why labour is divided at all, and why species differ in the mechanism used to produce different phenotypes - genetic differences, environmental cues, or random assignment of roles.

Four of the seven are invisible to all four retrieval conditions at k=20 under this paraphrase wording, so the cell separates conditions that generalise from ones that match strings. The survey label is honest because the answer is a structured account of the different levels at which the same question is attacked - a dimension every gold text supports and none of them states alone.

findings.claim: TEEPI (101024100) explains, at the level of gene expression, what makes an individual termite develop into a worker rather than a reproductive - the same explanandum as the gold set - and is excluded, while resiliANT is admitted on an equally result-level basis. Either TEEPI is an eighth gold member or the scope rule is being applied asymmetrically; the level does not move (|gold| stays >= 5, L3) either way.
findings.evidence: get_project_text(101024100) finalResults, verbatim: 'TEEPI project ... already unraveled the role of transposons during the adaptation to eusociality in termites, by enabling shifts of gene expression leading to new and divergent phenotypes among worker and reproductive castes.' Compare the basis on which resiliANT is IN - get_project_text(741491) finalResults: 'we used this development, in combination with starvation of targeted workers, to establish a causal relationship between fat content and division of labour' - also a reported result, not the stated headline aim (objective is 'identify the collective mechanisms responsible for ... resilience'). The counter-argument, recorded by the critic because it is real: resiliANT's workPerformed Aim 1a is a project aim about role assignment ('a model that describes and predicts the ontogeny of ... the types of labour that each individual performs ... a low-maturity nurse state and a high-maturity forager state'), whereas TEEPI's caste clause is one sentence inside a project whose explanandum is transposon-driven phenotypic innovation in Blattodea. That asymmetry is defensible; it is a judgement call, not a mechanical outcome of the drafter's own stated rule.
findings.fix_direction: Advisory, and the slot has no fix round. Two bounded options: add 101024100 to gold_project_ids (7 -> 8, level unchanged, pooling_evidence.accepted updated in lockstep), or leave gold at 7 and record TEEPI explicitly in the OUT list with the reason that caste divergence is an instance of the transposon explanandum rather than the thing explained. The second is a notes-only change.

record.text: How do EU-funded research projects go about explaining what decides which role an individual ends up taking inside an insect colony?
record.reference_answer: Seven projects treat the assignment of roles inside an insect society as the thing to be explained, and they attack it at very different levels. Genomic and molecular work dominates: RoyalMess searches for the genes that fate a Messor ant embryo to become a queen or a worker under social hybridogenesis; MELCA uses the double-clonal longhorn crazy ant Paratrechina longicornis to separate the molecular signatures of sex from those of the queen-versus-worker caste; and CASTECON asks whether inter-caste genetic correlations stop queens and workers from each reaching their own optimal dimorphic phenotype, and whether queens manipulate worker phenotype in their own interests. Physiology and neurobiology supply a second angle: DRiveR tests whether dopamine carries the Queen Mandibular Pheromone (QMP) signal that inhibits ovary activity in honeybee workers, while resiliANT measured the lipid content of individual ants by Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and, with targeted starvation, established a causal relationship between fat content and division of labour. MechAnt takes a mechanical view, tying the cutting ability of differently-sized leaf-cutter workers to the ontogeny of task choice and testing whether leaf-cutter colonies are organised according to ergonomic criteria. Division is the broadest: it asks across species why labour is divided at all, and why species differ in the mechanism used to produce different phenotypes - genetic differences, environmental cues, or random assignment of roles.

Scope rule applied to every candidate: IN iff the project's own text makes the assignment of roles inside an insect society (which individuals reproduce vs. which work, or which workers do which task) the thing being EXPLAINED, rather than a given used to explain something else. IN: 695744 CASTECON (caste dimorphism, queen-worker coadaptation, queens manipulating worker phenotype); 741491 resiliANT (fat content causally linked to division of labour; task preference of ant workers); 750766 MELCA (molecular mechanisms governing queen vs worker caste differences); 752656 DRiveR (QMP/dopamine repression of worker reproduction); 834164 Division (explains why and how labour is divided, incl. an across-species study on insects and the mechanism of role assignment); 851705 MechAnt (ontogeny of task choice of differently-sized workers, adaptive value of physical castes, ergonomic colony organisation); 948688 RoyalMess (genetic caste determination, caste-determining genes). OUT under the same rule: 660976 BrainiAnts (explanandum = brain structure/metabolic cost); 706208 SocParPhenoEvol (phenotypic diversity across parasite/host wasp species); 851523 EPIDEMIC and 771402 EPIDEMICSonCHIP and 802628 DISEASE and 771349 DEFEAT (task role is the explanatory variable for infection risk, not the explanandum); 842592 EvolvAnt and 840185 ConvergeAnt (queen number transitions, a colony-level trait); 893244 Ceratina (evolution of sociality across species); 101024100 TEEPI (transposable elements and Blattodea radiation); 101028937 WASSUP (solitary wasps - no colony members to assign roles to); 770964 ANTSolve (collective transport); 659106 GROUPIND (individual vs group personality in ants and starlings); 850859 ECOLBEH (wild birds); 708832 JHSIGNAL (juvenile hormone receptor, Drosophila); 638873 BeeDanceGap (dance communication); 648032 DBA and 654724 GROUPCOG (algorithmic/pigeon collective cognition); 760342 IoBee, 773921 PoshBee (bee health monitoring); 796025 Mesophotic, 101024448 STASIS (false LIKE hits). why_good: The question discriminates on whether a system can pool projects that share a research question but share almost no vocabulary: 'eusocial' reaches only 9 of the 34 projects in this theme, and the seven gold projects describe the same explanandum as caste determination, genetic caste fating, pheromonal reproductive repression, fat-driven task preference, worker-size biomechanics, and cross-species division-of-labour theory. Four of the seven are invisible to all four retrieval conditions at k=20 under this paraphrase wording, so the cell separates conditions that generalise from ones that match strings. It fills the biological-sciences bucket on the L3 survey axis with a paraphrase term_style, and the L3 label is arithmetic: |gold| = 7. The survey label is honest because the answer is a structured account of the different levels at which the same question is attacked - a dimension every gold text supports and none of them states alone.

findings.ruling_why: The critic's executed evidence is real - TEEPI's finalResults does speak to what makes a termite develop into a worker rather than a reproductive - but the critic also supplied, from evidence it executed, the ground that separates it from resiliANT: resiliANT's workPerformed Aim 1a makes the ontogeny of which labour each individual performs a project aim, whereas TEEPI's caste clause is one sentence inside a project whose explanandum is transposon-driven phenotypic innovation; that is a defensible application of the recorded scope rule, not an inconsistent one, so it is a marginal-boundary note that rides into the report for the user's promote-time veto and is never re-ruled.

judge_decisions.rationale: The cross-candidate stop rule fires when the same class has KILLED two candidates, and MISSED-GOLD has killed one here; on this candidate it arrives as a single MID on one arguable eighth member whose exclusion the critic itself calls defensible, which is not a kill. The distinction that matters is behavioural, not nominal: candidate 0's boundary moved on every adversarial pass because its scope sentence did not match the set it produced, while here two vocabulary channels the drafter never used (32-row objective regex, 14-row report regex, every unfamiliar name read in full) plus two independent retrievals returned no new satisfier, so the boundary reads closed and one contested edge case is what a hard survey boundary looks like when it is working. What the cell measures survives: |gold| = 7 holds L3 either way, the reference traces verbatim, the explanandum rule held mechanically against the eight closest OUTs, and the critic's reformulations put 5 of 7 gold in top-20 with conditions still separating - a hard paraphrase, which is what this cell is for, not an unmeasurable one. The judge would have accepted this package on a candidate with a fix round in hand; the exhausted budget neither lowers nor raises the bar.
